extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, neuroesthetics researchers, and mathematicians interested in fMRI studies of aesthetic experience
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and reporting an fMRI experiment in which expert subjects rate the beauty and understanding of mathematical formulae to identify neural correlates of aesthetic experience; includes behavioral measures, stimulus balancing, imaging acquisition, and statistical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection, consent, and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit subjects with appropriate expertise and screen for confounds; obtain written informed consent and ethics approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from study: sixteen mathematicians (postgraduate or postdoctoral level, 3 females, age range 22–32 years, 1 left-handed) recruited from colleges in London; all gave written informed consent and the study was approved by the Ethics Committee of University College London. One subject was eliminated after it transpired he had ADHD and was medicated. Also recruited 12 non-mathematicians for questionnaire-only data. Ensure normal or corrected vision. Document exclusions and note that exclusion did not affect overall results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and pre-screening (beauty pre-ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide subjects with the full stimulus set well before scanning and obtain detailed pre-scan ratings to inform stimulus sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this study each subject was given 60 mathematical formulae ~2–3 weeks before scanning to study at leisure and rate on a scale of −5 (ugly) to +5 (beautiful). Pre-scan ratings were used to assemble three groups (20 low, 20 medium, 20 high) individually for each subject to balance stimuli across scan sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral rating scales and post-scan measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear, numeric scales for different constructs and collect post-scan subjective measures to dissociate related constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty: pre-scan −5 to +5; scan-time: categorical Ugly/Neutral/Beautiful (coded −1,0,1). Understanding: post-scan rating 0 (no understanding) to 3 (profound understanding). Also include post-scan questionnaires about emotional responses. Use these measures both to sequence stimuli and as parametric modulators in fMRI analysis to separate effects of beauty and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus presentation and display control
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify and control display hardware, resolution, luminance, font, colors, and visual angles to ensure stimulus consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stimuli generated using Cogent 2000 and back-projected via an Epson EH-TW5910 at 1600×1200, 60 Hz, onto a translucent screen (290×180 mm). Equations drawn in same sized font in white (CIE 1931 XYZ: 755, 761, 637) on same gray background (CIE 1931 XYZ: 236, 228, 200). Screen brightness varied between 280 and 324 cd m−2; equation widths and heights given in visual angle (4°–24° width, 1°–5° height).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental timing, session structure and counterbalancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define trial structure, session timing, and pseudo-randomization to balance conditions and baseline acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four functional scanning sessions; 15 equations per session so each of 60 equations appears once. Each session: 19.5 s initial blank, 15 trials of 16 s each, interspersed with four blanks of 16–17 s; session ends with 30 s blank (≈7 min 20 s per session). Each trial: equation displayed 16 s, 1 s blank, 3 s response screen (subjects press one of three buttons), followed by 1–2 s inter-trial blank. Pre-scan beauty ratings used to ensure 5 low, 5 medium, 5 high rated equations per session where possible; pseudo-randomized so a low-rated equation never directly follows another low-rated one (same for medium/high).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unequal category counts and missing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and accommodate imbalances in subject-generated category counts; discuss effect on efficiency and inference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study notes fewer 'Ugly' ratings and occasional sessions with no 'Ugly' ratings (e.g., two sessions had no Ugly). They state that imbalance reduces estimation efficiency but does not bias estimation or inference (Friston et al., 2000). Document ratios per session (Tables provided) and evaluate whether relationships can still be established despite missing categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition parameters and anatomical imaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Report scanner model, coil, fieldmap acquisition, sequence parameters, slice coverage, voxel size, and anatomical scan details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example parameters: 3-T Siemens Magnetom Trio with 32-channel head coil; B0 fieldmap via double-echo FLASH (duration 2'14"). EPI for functional scans measuring BOLD (reported TE = 30 ms, TR = 68 ms, volume time = 3.264 s), 48 axial slices 2 mm thick with 1 mm gap, voxel resolution 3×3×3 mm covering nearly whole brain. Anatomical: T1 MDEFT sagittal, 176 slices isotropic 1 mm, TE = 2.48 ms, TR = 7.92 ms. Provide full details so others can replicate acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing and statistical analysis software
rubrics_metrics.description: State the analysis package and versions used and reference relevant methodological sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This work used SPM8 (Statistical Parametric Mapping) and follows procedures from prior related studies (Zeki and Romaya, 2010; Ishizu and Zeki, 2011). Reference canonical texts/methods (Friston et al., 2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling strategy: parametric modulators and orthogonalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Model continuous subjective measures as parametric modulators and use orthogonalization to partition variance between correlated modulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At single-subject level, include understanding rating (0–3) and scan-time beauty rating (−1,0,1) as first and second parametric modulators of a boxcar modeling appearance of each equation. Because beauty and understanding correlated but imperfectly, orthogonalization in SPM allows beauty modulator to capture variance not explained by understanding (and vice versa in alternate models), enabling separation of 'beauty only' and 'understanding only' components. Note that a common portion of variance remains unassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice between parametric and categorical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand differences in sensitivity and interpretability between parametric vs categorical contrasts and use both where informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parametric analysis looks for relationships between BOLD signal and graded ratings across sessions; categorical analysis averages BOLD for discrete categories over sessions and subjects. Orthogonalization to partition variance is available only in parametric analyses. The authors used parametric analyses to identify relationships and categorical analyses to extract parameter estimates for Ugly/Neutral/Beautiful or understanding categories, acknowledging categorical analyses' lower sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical thresholding, multiple comparison correction and reporting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear whole-brain correction strategies and report thresholds, cluster extents, and familywise error statistics; report coordinates in a standard space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary contrasts reported at cluster-level significance P_Clust-FWE < 0.05 with familywise error correction over whole brain (based on random field theory). Clusters defined with a background voxelwise threshold P_unc < 0.001 and extent threshold of 10 voxels. Other, non-principal contrasts reported at peak-voxel threshold P_FWE < 0.05. Provide MNI coordinates for peaks, cluster sizes (kE), t-values, and P_FWE, and explicitly note activations that did not reach significance but are reported as suggestive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjunction analyses and overlap interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conjunction-null analyses to test overlap between contrasts and interpret overlap with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study used a conjunction-null analysis (Nichols et al., 2005) to determine overlap within mOFC between parametric activations with beauty and de-activations produced by viewing equations. Both contrasts were thresholded at P_unc < 0.001. Use such analyses to infer overlapping subregions but be explicit about thresholds and the inferential logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting activation, de-activation and interpretive caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Report both activations and de-activations relative to baseline and clarify that 'activation' can mean relative increase within an overall deactivated region; annotate exploratory or non-significant findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note that mOFC showed parametric increases with beauty even though the region was deactivated relative to baseline overall—i.e., a relative activation in a deactivated region. They also documented several areas that did not reach cluster-level significance but may contribute and left them for future studies. Clearly distinguish primary from exploratory findings and indicate their statistical status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral data analysis and integration with imaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and report behavioral distributions, correlations, and how they inform imaging contrasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide frequency distributions of pre-scan, scan-time beauty, and understanding ratings. Compute correlations (e.g., Pearson's r) between pre-scan and scan-time beauty ratings and between understanding and beauty to assess separability (the study reports r = 0.612 and r = 0.413 respectively). Use behavioral imbalance statistics to assess feasibility of session-wise contrasts and to motivate modeling choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and reference supplementary data files containing stimuli, rating forms, and raw behavioral data to enable replication and reanalysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This article supplies Data Sheets: EquationsForm.pdf (questionnaire), UnderstandingForm.pdf, BehavioralData.xlsx (tables of behavioral data including per-subject ratings and trial sequences), and BeauNeutUglyBase.pdf (tables of categorical beauty activations vs baseline). Link to supplementary material location in the article and make raw tables available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and conflict of interest disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare ethical approvals, funding sources, and conflicts of interest (or absence thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state ethics committee approval, funding acknowledgments (e.g., Wellcome Trust Strategic Award), and a conflict-of-interest statement (authors declared absence of commercial/financial conflicts). Include corresponding author contact information for data or materials requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive linkage between domain-specific understanding and aesthetic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Design analyses to dissociate domain-specific understanding from aesthetic experience and discuss theoretical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This study modeled understanding ratings and beauty ratings as separate modulators and interpreted mOFC activity as parametrically related to beauty after accounting for understanding. They discuss implications (e.g., beauty not strictly tied to understanding) and caution that separating these constructs has limits; use both neuroimaging and behavioral data to support theoretical claims.
